# Nomadar and Cádiz CF to Hold Their First Youth Soccer Camp in Uruguay in January


by[Press](https://nomadar.com/author/press/)


| Nov 10, 2026


|[News](https://nomadar.com/category/news/) |[0 comments](https://nomadar.com/nomadar-y-el-cadiz-cf-celebraran-en-enero-su-primer-campus-de-futbol-base-en-uruguay-2/#respond)


Nomadar and Cádiz CF are taking the HPT (High Performance Training) program to Uruguay. From January 11 to 15, 2027, Punta del Este will host the Cádiz CF–Nomadar International Campus, the first youth soccer camp Nomadar has organized in the country.


About 100 young players, ages 8 and older, are expected to take part. For five days, they will train with Cádiz CF coaches and see firsthand how Spanish professional soccer works.


The camp does not end after five days of training. Two of the players who stand out the most will be selected to travel to Cádiz in April 2027 and train for one week with the club.


Pablo Sánchez, Head of International at Cádiz CF and Director of International Sports Projects at Nomadar, says the goal is to give young players the same training philosophy and professional standards used in Cádiz, in a country with a strong soccer tradition.


Local coordination is led by Kilómetro Deportivo, a Uruguayan organization focused on youth development and international sports experiences. Its representative, Guillermo Cabana, says that bringing the Cádiz CF and Nomadar experience to Uruguay is a great opportunity for players and their families.


In Cabana’s view, soccer opens doors to new experiences, learning, and personal growth, and the camp will let participants train with professional coaches, see a different soccer culture, and build connections beyond the field. He sees it as the start of a long-term relationship.


The camp builds on the experience of the HPT (High Performance Training) program, which has welcomed more than 350 young players over the past three years from the United States, Japan, Mexico, Germany, Ecuador, Nigeria, and Azerbaijan. Some of them have been called up to national teams: Mario Lobato to the Spain U15 National Team and Jan Saltzman to the Sweden U17 National Team.


With Uruguay, Nomadar adds a new market to its international youth soccer network, which connects the United States, Latin America, and Europe.


Technical preparations will start on December 21, 2026, with an online meeting between the Cádiz CF coaching staff and the Uruguayan organizers. They will finalize the training groups and the program logistics.
